objects.description: Opaque codec context managing all state and resources for compression and decompression. Actual layout is hidden; create with astcenc_context_alloc() and destroy with astcenc_context_free(). Thread-safe usage follows the documented threading model; one context processes one image at a time.

objects.definition:
enum astcenc_error {
	ASTCENC_SUCCESS = 0,
	ASTCENC_ERR_OUT_OF_MEM,
	ASTCENC_ERR_BAD_CPU_FLOAT,
	ASTCENC_ERR_BAD_PARAM,
	ASTCENC_ERR_BAD_BLOCK_SIZE,
	ASTCENC_ERR_BAD_PROFILE,
	ASTCENC_ERR_BAD_QUALITY,
	ASTCENC_ERR_BAD_SWIZZLE,
	ASTCENC_ERR_BAD_FLAGS,
	ASTCENC_ERR_BAD_CONTEXT,
	ASTCENC_ERR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED,
	ASTCENC_ERR_BAD_DECODE_MODE,
#if defined(ASTCENC_DIAGNOSTICS)
	ASTCENC_ERR_DTRACE_FAILURE,
#endif
};
objects.description: Result/status code enumeration returned by API calls. Values cover success, parameter validation failures, unsupported operations, and build-conditional diagnostic failures.
Color profile used for encoding/decoding which controls transfer characteristics and decode mode behavior.
Component selector enum for swizzling image channels or constants, including a reconstructed normal Z.
Per-channel swizzle describing how to map source/decoded components; used by compress/decompress calls.
Texel component storage type for uncompressed images: 8-bit UNORM, 16-bit float, or 32-bit float.
Function pointer type for optional progress reporting callback. Receives progress percent in [0,100]. Called from a worker thread.

Compressor configuration controlling color profile, flags, block size, error weighting, tuning limits, and optional progress callback. Initialize via astcenc_config_init() and optionally tweak before allocating a context.

Uncompressed 2D/3D image container passed to compressor/decompressor. Holds dimensions, component type, and an array of pointers to tightly-packed 2D slices (length dim_z). Data is 4 components per texel.

Metadata description of a single ASTC 16-byte block’s encoding, populated by astcenc_get_block_info(). Useful for debugging and analysis. Non-applicable fields are zeroed for error or constant blocks.

functions.name: astcenc_config_init
functions.signature: ASTCENC_PUBLIC astcenc_error astcenc_config_init(astcenc_profile profile, unsigned int block_x, unsigned int block_y, unsigned int block_z, float quality, unsigned int flags, astcenc_config* config)
functions.description: Populate an astcenc_config with defaults and validated parameters for a given color profile, ASTC block size, quality preset/effort, and flags. Typical use is to call this once per desired configuration, optionally tweak advanced fields in the returned config, and then pass it to astcenc_context_alloc.
requirements: config must be a valid, writable pointer.
profile must be one of astcenc_profile values.
block_x, block_y, block_z must form a valid ASTC block size (function may return ASTCENC_ERR_BAD_BLOCK_SIZE for invalid sizes).
quality should be an ASTCENC_PRE_* preset or an effort value in [0, 100]; out-of-spec may return ASTCENC_ERR_BAD_QUALITY.
flags must contain only ASTCENC_FLG_* bits defined by ASTCENC_ALL_FLAGS; otherwise ASTCENC_ERR_BAD_FLAGS.
Callers must check the returned astcenc_error and not use the config if it is not ASTCENC_SUCCESS.

functions.name: astcenc_context_alloc
functions.signature: ASTCENC_PUBLIC astcenc_error astcenc_context_alloc(const astcenc_config* config, unsigned int thread_count, astcenc_context** context)
functions.description: Allocate a codec context using a previously prepared astcenc_config, creating all internal resources and worker state for the specified thread_count. Reuse the returned context to process multiple images serially to amortize setup cost.
requirements: config must point to a config previously initialized (typically via astcenc_config_init) and optionally tuned.
If building a decompress-only library (ASTCENC_DECOMPRESS_ONLY), config->flags must include ASTCENC_FLG_DECOMPRESS_ONLY; otherwise allocation will fail.
thread_count must match intended concurrent callers of compress/decompress (each caller will use a unique thread_index in [0, thread_count-1]).
context must be a valid, writable pointer that will receive the allocated astcenc_context* on success.
Callers must check the returned astcenc_error; allocation can fail with ASTCENC_ERR_OUT_OF_MEM or other errors.
Contexts configured with ASTCENC_FLG_DECOMPRESS_ONLY do not support compression calls (those calls will fail).

functions.name: astcenc_compress_image
functions.signature: ASTCENC_PUBLIC astcenc_error astcenc_compress_image(astcenc_context* context, astcenc_image* image, const astcenc_swizzle* swizzle, uint8_t* data_out, size_t data_len, unsigned int thread_index)
functions.description: Compress an image into ASTC blocks using the provided context. For multithreaded contexts, call this from N threads with unique thread_index values; work is internally scheduled. The swizzle is applied to input image components prior to compression. Output is written to data_out.
requirements: context must be a valid context created by astcenc_context_alloc and not configured as decompress-only (otherwise ASTCENC_ERR_BAD_CONTEXT or operation failure).
Exactly one image may be in-flight per context at a time; coordinate multithreaded calls via thread_index as documented.
image must be initialized: dim_x, dim_y, dim_z set; data_type set to ASTCENC_TYPE_U8/F16/F32; data must point to an array of dim_z 2D slices, each tightly packed as described in the header.
swizzle must be a valid, non-null pointer specifying component selection for compression.
data_out must point to a writable buffer of size data_len bytes.

data_len must be large enough for the entire compressed image; ASTC uses fixed 16-byte blocks, so required size is ceil(dim_x/block_x) * ceil(dim_y/block_y) * ceil(dim_z/block_z) * 16 bytes (inferred from API and ASTC spec). The function may fail if undersized (e.g., ASTCENC_ERR_OUT_OF_MEM).
thread_index must be unique per calling thread and in [0, configured_thread_count-1].
Callers must check the returned astcenc_error and handle non-success.
For contexts configured for multi-threading, callers are responsible for synchronization across images and must call astcenc_compress_reset between images as documented.

functions.name: astcenc_compress_reset
functions.description: Reset a context’s compression state so it can be used to compress the next image. Required when using multithreaded compression between images; optional but harmless for single-threaded contexts.
requirements: context must be a valid context created by astcenc_context_alloc.
Must only be called once all threads have exited astcenc_compress_image for image N, and before any thread enters it for image N+1.
Callers must ensure proper thread synchronization around this call.
Callers must check the returned astcenc_error.

functions.name: astcenc_compress_cancel
functions.description: Request cancellation of any ongoing compression on the context. The compressed data becomes undefined; the caller must still complete normal synchronization and reset before starting another compression.
requirements: context must be a valid context created by astcenc_context_alloc.
After cancellation, the caller must behave as if compression completed for synchronization purposes and must call astcenc_compress_reset before starting another compression.
Callers must check the returned astcenc_error.

functions.name: astcenc_decompress_image
functions.signature: ASTCENC_PUBLIC astcenc_error astcenc_decompress_image(astcenc_context* context, const uint8_t* data, size_t data_len, astcenc_image* image_out, const astcenc_swizzle* swizzle, unsigned int thread_index)
functions.description: Decompress ASTC-compressed data into an output image buffer using the provided context. For multithreaded contexts, any subset of threads can call this with unique thread_index values. The swizzle is applied after decompression to map decoded components to the output layout.
requirements: context must be a valid context created by astcenc_context_alloc (decompression is supported for both full and decompress-only contexts).
data must point to the compressed image data and remain valid for the duration of the call.

data_len must match the size of the compressed image; ASTC uses 16-byte blocks, so expected size is ceil(dim_x/block_x) * ceil(dim_y/block_y) * ceil(dim_z/block_z) * 16 bytes for the target image dimensions (inferred from API and ASTC spec).
image_out must be initialized with target dimensions and data_type; its data must point to an array of dim_z writable 2D slices, tightly packed as documented.
swizzle must be a valid, non-null pointer specifying component mapping applied after decompression.
thread_index must be unique per calling thread and in [0, configured_thread_count-1].
Only one image may be in-flight per context at a time; callers must use astcenc_decompress_reset between images in multithreaded scenarios.
Callers must check the returned astcenc_error.

functions.name: astcenc_decompress_reset
functions.description: Reset a context’s decompression state so it can be used for the next image in multithreaded workflows. Optional for single-threaded use.
requirements: context must be a valid context created by astcenc_context_alloc.
Must only be called once all threads have exited astcenc_decompress_image for image N, and before any thread enters it for image N+1.
Callers must ensure proper thread synchronization around this call.
Callers must check the returned astcenc_error.

functions.name: astcenc_context_free
functions.description: Free all resources associated with a codec context allocated by astcenc_context_alloc.
requirements: context must be a context previously returned by astcenc_context_alloc. Passing invalid pointers results in undefined behavior (null handling is not documented).
Do not use the context after this call.

functions.name: astcenc_get_block_info
functions.signature: ASTCENC_PUBLIC astcenc_error astcenc_get_block_info(astcenc_context* context, const uint8_t data[16], astcenc_block_info* info)
functions.description: Decode one 16-byte ASTC block’s metadata into an astcenc_block_info summary. Useful for analysis and tooling. Returns success even if the block payload encodes an error block, as long as decoding completed.
requirements: context must be a valid context created by astcenc_context_alloc.
data must point to exactly 16 bytes of ASTC block data.
info must be a valid, writable pointer to receive results.
Callers must check the returned astcenc_error.

functions.name: astcenc_get_error_string
functions.description: Return a human-readable, null-terminated string describing the given astcenc_error status code.
requirements: status must be a value from astcenc_error.
The returned pointer remains valid for at least the lifetime of the library; treat it as read-only.

data_types.description: Arbitrary uninterpreted byte sequences. The fuzzer-provided std::string is treated as a byte buffer and copied/modulo-wrapped into target buffers (image slices or compressed-data buffers) without any required encoding or structure. Any 0–255 byte values are valid; not required to be text or follow any format.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator targets fuzz stubs that use FUZZ_PARAM_STR as a repeating
# byte pattern to fill various buffers (image slices, compressed data, 16-byte blocks).
# The stubs treat the data type as raw binary bytes with no structure, so any
# non-empty byte string is valid. We generate seeded, varied patterns intended to
# exercise different code paths (e.g., constant blocks, gradients, high entropy,
# small/large lengths, alignment-sensitive lengths), while keeping the overall
# size under 4096 bytes.

MAX_LEN = 4096

# A set of interesting byte sequences to exercise different behaviors when wrapped
# over varying buffer sizes by the stubs.
INTERESTING_PATTERNS: List[bytes] = [
    b"\x00",  # all zeros when repeated
    b"\xFF",  # all 0xFF when repeated
    b"\x80",  # midpoint single byte
    b"\x00\xFF",  # alternating extremes
    b"\x00\x00\x00\xFF",  # mostly zero with spikes
    b"\xFF\x00\xFF\x00",  # alternating inverse
    b"\x00\x01\x02\x03\x04\x05\x06\x07",  # ascending small ramp
    bytes(range(16)),  # 0..15 (matches ASTC block size periodicity)
    bytes(range(32)),  # 0..31 to test non-power-of-two wrap
    b"ASTCENC\x00TEST\xFF",  # mixed ASCII + sentinels
]

# Generate smooth ramps for potential gradient-like content in images

def make_ramp(length: int, start: int, step: int, mod: int = 256) -> bytes:
    return bytes(((start + i * step) % mod) for i in range(length))

# Generate repeating short patterns with prime lengths to create nontrivial wrapping

def make_prime_pattern(p: int) -> bytes:
    base = bytes((i * 37 + 13) % 256 for i in range(p))
    return base

# High entropy but deterministic pseudo-random block

def make_prng_block(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(length))

# Construct a palette pattern: repeating small set of values

def make_palette(values: List[int], repeat: int) -> bytes:
    seq = bytes(values)
    return (seq * max(1, repeat))[: len(seq) * max(1, repeat)]

# Core generator for FUZZ_PARAM_STR content

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a target size. FUZZ stubs modulo-wrap our string over varied buffer
    # sizes, so we keep this reasonably small but vary it to hit alignment edges.
    # Bias towards sizes that interact with 16-byte ASTC block size and common texel sizes.
    candidate_sizes = [
        1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 12, 15, 16, 17, 24, 31, 32, 48, 63, 64, 127, 128, 191, 192, 255, 256
    ]
    # Occasionally pick a random size up to 512 to diversify, but never exceed MAX_LEN.
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        candidate_sizes.append(rng.randint(5, 512))
    size = min(MAX_LEN, rng.choice(candidate_sizes))

    chunks: List[bytes] = []

    # Always include at least one deterministic high-entropy chunk of a prime length
    prime_lengths = [17, 19, 23, 29, 31]
    pl = rng.choice(prime_lengths)
    chunks.append(make_prng_block(rng, pl))

    # Add one or two interesting fixed patterns
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 2)):
        chunks.append(rng.choice(INTERESTING_PATTERNS))

    # Add a ramp or inverse ramp
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        step = rng.choice([1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 11])
        start = rng.randrange(256)
        ramp_len = rng.choice([8, 12, 16, 24, 32])
        ramp = make_ramp(ramp_len, start, step)
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            ramp = bytes(reversed(ramp))
        chunks.append(ramp)

    # Add a palette-based pattern (e.g., 4 or 16 levels), useful for image data types
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        levels = rng.choice([[0, 255], [0, 85, 170, 255], [0, 64, 128, 192, 255]])
        repeat = rng.randint(2, 8)
        chunks.append(make_palette(levels, repeat))

    # Add a prime-length repeated pattern to encourage complex wrap when copied
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        p = rng.choice([13, 17, 19, 23, 29])
        chunks.append(make_prime_pattern(p))

    # Optionally insert a small header-like prefix with markers; not required by API
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        tag = b"ASTC" + struct.pack("<I", rng.getrandbits(32))
        chunks.insert(0, tag)

    # Concatenate and trim/pad to requested size
    buf = b"".join(chunks)

    # Ensure non-empty; if empty fallback to a single zero
    if not buf:
        buf = b"\x00"

    # Trim or extend to size by repetition; the stubs will modulo-wrap anyway,
    # but providing the exact size keeps behavior deterministic and bounded.
    if len(buf) < size:
        # Repeat the buffer until size reached
        reps = (size + len(buf) - 1) // len(buf)
        buf = (buf * reps)[:size]
    else:
        buf = buf[:size]

    # Final safety: cap to MAX_LEN
    if len(buf) > MAX_LEN:
        buf = buf[:MAX_LEN]

    return buf
